signature.name: VTask.limitRecOn
signature.type: {motive : Ordinal.{u_5} → Sort u_4} -> (o : Ordinal.{u_5}) -> (zero : motive 0) -> (add_one : (o : Ordinal.{u_5}) → motive o → motive (o + 1)) -> (limit : (o : Ordinal.{u_5}) → Order.IsSuccLimit o → ((o' : Ordinal.{u_5}) → o' < o → motive o') → motive o) -> motive o

conventions.statement: When o = 0, VTask.limitRecOn o zero add_one limit computes to zero.
conventions.note: Base case; 0 is not treated as a limit ordinal.

conventions.statement: When o = a + 1 for some ordinal a, VTask.limitRecOn o zero add_one limit computes to add_one a (VTask.limitRecOn a zero add_one limit).
conventions.note: Successor step unfolds one layer of recursion.

conventions.statement: When o is a limit ordinal (Order.IsSuccLimit o holds, meaning o ≠ 0 and o is not a successor), VTask.limitRecOn o zero add_one limit computes to limit o h (fun o' _ => VTask.limitRecOn o' zero add_one limit).
conventions.note: The limit step receives access to all recursively computed values at smaller ordinals.

conventions.statement: The ordinal 0 is handled by the zero case, not the limit case, even though it has no predecessor; Order.IsSuccLimit 0 is false in Mathlib's convention.
conventions.note: This is a deliberate split: the three branches are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
